column5: wild; dog; wild dog; wild animal(s), game; hunting dog
column6: From Proto-Celtic *weidus (“wild”) + *ᚉᚒᚅᚐ (*cuna, “dog”). The name could therefore mean “wild dog”, but in Old Irish fíad had come to mean “wild animal(s), game” and many of its derivatives refer to hunting.

From *ᚉᚒᚅᚐ (*cuna, “dog”) + *ᚋᚐᚌᚂᚔ (*magli, “chief”).

From Proto-Celtic *enīkʷom (“face”) + *glastos (“green, blue”).

Compound of *ᚺᚨᚦᚢᛉ (*haþuʀ, “war, battle”) + *ᛚᚨᛁᚲᚨᛉ (*laikaʀ, “play, sport”). The first element may also be *ᚺᚨᛞᚢᛉ (*haduʀ /⁠handuʀ⁠/, “hand”), with non-writing of a nasal before a homorganic consonant.

*ᚺᛖᚱᚢᛉ (*heruʀ, “sword”) + *ᚹᚢᛚᚠᚨᛉ (*wulfaʀ, “wolf”).

Inherited from Proto-Germanic *Swēbaharjaz, equivalent to *ᛊᚹᚨᛒᚨᛉ (*swabaʀ, “Swebian”) + *ᚺᚨᚱᛃᚨᛉ (*harjaʀ, “warrior”). Compare Old English Swǣfhere, Old High German Suābheri.
ᛊᛏᚨᛁᚾᚨᛉ (stainaʀ, “stone”) + *ᚹᚨᚱᛃᚨᛉ (*warjaʀ, “defender”). Compare ᛒᛁᛞᚨᚹᚨᚱᛁᛃᚨᛉ (bidawarijaʀ) with same second element.

*ᛚᚨᛞᚨ (*lada /⁠landa⁠/, “land”) + *ᚹᚨᚱᛃᚨᛉ (*warjaʀ, “defender, guardian”). Compare ᛒᛁᛞᚨᚹᚨᚱᛁᛃᚨᛉ (bidawarijaʀ) and ᛊᛏᚨᛁᚾᚨᚹᚨᚱᛁᛃᚨᛉ (stainawarijaʀ) with same second element.

From Old Persian 𐎭𐎠𐎼𐎹𐎺𐎢𐏁 (d-a-r-y-v-u-š), compare Egyptian ini-ti-rw-i-i-wA-SA (jntjrwywꜣšꜣ).
Possibly from Proto-Italic *aljos, in which case the term is cognate with Latin alius.

From 𐌰𐌻𐌻𐍃 (alls, “all”) + 𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (reiks, “king, ruler”), from Proto-Germanic *Alarīks. Cognate to Old English Alrīca, Old Norse Alríkr, Alrekr.
From the Proto-Germanic elements *bataz (“good”) + *winiz (“friend”). It is uncertain whether this is a Proto-Germanic formation or whether the name postdates Proto-Germanic.
From *𐌲𐌰𐌹𐍃 (*gais, “spear”) + 𐌻𐌰𐌹𐌺𐍃 (laiks, “dance”). Cognate with German Gerlach.
From 𐌲𐌿𐌸 (guþ, “god”) + *𐍆𐍂𐌹𐌸𐌿𐍃 (*friþus, “peace”).
Unclear, possibly from 𐌲𐌿𐌸 (guþ, “God”) + *𐌻𐌿𐌱𐍉 (*lubō, “love”) (from *lubō), or with a second element 𐌻𐌹𐌿𐍆𐍃 (liufs, “dear”) (thus meaning dear to God).
From Ancient Greek Δαμιανός (Damianós); compare English Damian.
From Proto-Germanic *Hrōþirīks; equivalent to *𐌷𐍂𐍉𐌸𐍃 (*hrōþs, “glory”) + 𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (reiks, “ruler”).
From Proto-Germanic *Þeudōrīks. By surface analysis, 𐌸𐌹𐌿𐌳𐌰 (þiuda, “people, nation”) + 𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (reiks, “king, ruler”).
From *𐌼𐌴𐍂𐍃 (*mērs, “fame”) + -𐌹𐌻𐌰 (-ila).
The second element is taken to be 𐌷𐌰𐍂𐌾𐌹𐍃 (harjis), more specifically the stem -𐌷𐌰𐍂𐌹. The cause of the loss of final -(𐌹)𐍃 is unclear; the best explanation might simply be a dialectal change.

From 𐍃𐌿𐌽𐌾𐌰 (sunja, “truth”) + *𐍆𐍂𐌹𐌸𐌿𐍃 (*friþus, “peace”). Why the attested form ends in -as is unclear, but compare the similarly non-Ulfilan form 𐍆𐍂𐌹𐌸𐌰𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐌴𐌹𐍃 (friþareikeis); this may be due to dialectal differences between Ulfilan Goth…
From 𐍃𐍅𐌹𐌽𐌸𐍃 (swinþs, “strong”) + -𐌹𐌻𐌰 (-ila).

May be from earlier *𐍅𐌴𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐌰 (*wēreika), where the first part probably corresponds to *𐍅𐌴𐍂𐌴𐌹 (*wērei, “truth”) (as found in the word 𐌰𐌻𐌻𐌰𐍅𐌴𐍂𐌴𐌹 (allawērei)). from *𐍅𐌴𐍂𐍃 (*wērs) + -𐌴𐌹 (-ei). The change of 𐌴𐌹 to 𐌴 in the spelling of…

From 𐍅𐌹𐌻𐌾𐌰 (wilja, “will, desire”) + *𐍂𐌴𐌸𐍃 (*rēþs, “counsel”) from Proto-Germanic *rēdaz; cf. Vandalic *rith, original East Germanic [e:] shifting to [i] in unstressed positions, in parallel with Greek and Latin iotacism.
From *𐍅𐌹𐍄𐌹 (*witi, “wit”) + 𐍂𐌴𐌹𐌺𐍃 (reiks, “ruler”).
From 𐍅𐌿𐌻𐍆𐍃 (wulfs, “wolf”) + -𐌹𐌻𐌰 (-ila, “diminutive suffix”). This form is reconstructed based on a variety of Greek and Latin spellings (see Descendants).
From Proto-Germanic *fardiz (“journey”) + *nanþaz (“ready”).
This single attested form is very likely inherited from Proto-Germanic *Friþurīks or is very closely related to that form.
From *𐍆𐍂𐌹𐌸𐌿𐍃 (*friþus, “peace”) + *𐌲𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌽𐍃 (*gairns, “eager”).
Second part is 𐎎𐎍𐎋 (mlk, “king”).

column5: Iranians; to calm down, to settle down, to become quiet; creating
column6: From 𐎠𐎼𐎡𐎹𐎠 (a-r-i-y-a /⁠Aryā⁠/, “Iranians”) + *ramnah (of unclear meaning): according to Mayrhofer and Tavernier, the second element means "peace," derived from *ram- (“to calm down, to settle down, to become quiet”); Schmitt prefers interpreting it as *H…
Unknown; possibly of Armenian (compare արքայ (arkʻay, “king”) or երախայ (eraxay, “child”)) or Urartian origin.
From Proto-Iranian *Hr̥taxšaθrah. Equivalent to 𐎠𐎼𐎫 (r̥taʰ, “Asha; truth”) + 𐎧𐏁𐏂𐎶 (xšaçam, “realm; reign”). Doublet of *R̥taxšaθrah, cognate with Parthian 𐭀𐭓𐭕𐭇𐭔𐭕𐭓 (ʾrtḥštr /⁠Ardaxšahr⁠/).

From *(w)r̥šā (“man; hero”) + -𐎣 (-k /⁠-kaʰ⁠/, hypocoristic suffix). First element alternatively from *r̥šah (“bear”), from Proto-Iranian *Hŕ̥šah. Cognate with Parthian 𐭀𐭓𐭔𐭊 (ʾršk /⁠Aršak⁠/).
From 𐎠𐎿𐎱 (a-s-p /⁠aspaʰ⁠/, “horse”) + *canāh (“desire”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čánHas (“desire”).
From *āçiš (“fire”) + *-inah (hypocoristic suffix). Cognate with Old Median *Āθrinah and Parthian 𐭀𐭕𐭓𐭉𐭍 (ʾtryn /⁠Āhrin⁠/).

Possibly from 𐎢 (u /⁠ʰu-⁠/, “good”) + *tānah (“tone, melody”), from Proto-Iranian *tā́nah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tā́nas, from Proto-Indo-European *tónos. Cognate with Sanskrit सुतान (sutā́na, “well-tuned, melodious”).

column5: cow; eating; where there is much to eat; lord, master

From *gauš (“cattle”) + *-mah (possessive suffix) + *-ātah (intensificative suffix). Compare with Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬊𐬨𐬀𐬧𐬙 (gaomaṇt).

From *darš (“to dare”). Cognate with Sanskrit दाधृषि (dādhṛṣi, “bold, courageous”).

From *θuxrah (“red, bright”). Cognate of Old Median *Suxrah.
From 𐏎 (BG /⁠bagaʰ⁠/, “god”) + *abignah (“attacking power”).

From Akkadian 𒀭𒀝𒈾𒀪𒀉 (ᵈAG-na-ʾ-id /⁠Nabû-naʾid⁠/, “May Nabu be exalted”).
From *maθištah. Cognate with Old Median *Masištah.
*mr̥duš (“mild, soft”) + 𐎴 (n /⁠-naʰ⁠/, nominal suffix) + 𐎡𐎹 (i-y /⁠-yaʰ⁠/, adjectival suffix). Compare with Sanskrit मृदुता (mṛdutā) and मृदुल (mṛdula).
From *vahyaz (“better”) + 𐎭𐎠𐎫𐎶 (d-a-t-m /⁠dātam⁠/, “law”).
From Proto-Iranian *WindáhuHarnāh. Cognate with Avestan 𐬬𐬌𐬜𐬀𐬝⸱𐬓𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬀𐬵 (viδat̰.xᵛar^ənah) and Parthian 𐭅𐭉𐭍𐭃𐭐𐭓𐭍 (wyndprn /⁠Windafarn⁠/).

Borrowed from Avestan 𐬬𐬌𐬱𐬙𐬁𐬯𐬞𐬀 (vištāspa). Equivalent to *vištah (“free, unbridled”) + 𐎠𐎿𐎱 (a-s-p /⁠aspaʰ⁠/, “horse”).
From *haxā (“friend, companion”) + *maniš (“thought, mind”).

Compound name of 𐤀𐤇 (ʾḥ, “brother”) + 𐤌𐤋𐤒𐤓𐤕 (mlqrt, “Melqart”).

column5: may he grace me; lord; grace

𐤏𐤁𐤃 (ʿbd, “slave, servant”) + 𐤀𐤋𐤀𐤁 (ʾlʾb, “Eliab”), yielding "Slave of Eliab". Compare Hebrew אֱלִיאָב (ʾĔlīʾāb).

Borrowed from Egyptian pꜣ-ꜥẖm (literally “The Cultic Falcon-Image”). Compare Sahidic Coptic ⲡⲁϩⲱⲙ (pahōm), Bohairic Coptic ⲡⲁϧⲱⲙ (paxōm) and Ancient Greek Παχουμις (Pakhoumis).

From Proto-Saka *aza (“leader”) (cf. Khotanese hinajha (“commander of army”)). Cognate with Ancient Greek Ἄζης (Ázēs).

column5: lady; girl; daughter of a minister

From Proto-Saka *Ārazāta (“noble-born”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese āra (“worthy, noble”) + a cognate of Khotanese ysātä (“born”)).
From Proto-Saka *arθya (“pious”). Compare with Avestan 𐬀𐬱𐬫𐬀 (ašya, “pious”).

column5: striving, ambitious, energetic; to seek, search
column6: From Proto-Saka *Kuzulaka (“striving, ambitious, energetic”). Compare with Khotanese [script needed] (kūys, “to seek, search”).

column5: who looks down upon the lust; lust; to survey, look down upon
column6: From Proto-Saka *Kāmauya (“who looks down upon the lust”), composed of Proto-Saka *kāma (“lust”) + a cognate of Khotanese uy (“to survey, look down upon”).
column7: Proto-Saka*Kāmauya (“who looks down upon the lust”)

column6: From Proto-Saka *kaluka (“noble”). Compare with Khotanese kala (“excellent”).
From Proto-Saka *Xārahōsta (“splendid, mighty”), composed of *xāra (“splendid”) + *hauvasta (“powerful”) (cf. Khotanese hauvasta (“powerful”).
From Proto-Saka *Xrataka (“wisdom”) (cf. Khotanese gratä (“instruction, advice”)), from Old Iranian *xratu (“wisdom”).
From Proto-Saka *Xāramasah (“splendid greatness”), composed of *xāra (“splendid”) + a cognate of Khotanese mase, from Proto-Saka *masāh (“greatness”).

column5: of shining face; splendid; shining; face
column6: From Proto-Saka *Xārašāmača (“of shining face”), composed of Scythian *xāra (“splendid”) (cf. Khotanese khāra in khārāva (“shining”)) + a cognate of Khotanese śśāman (“face”).

Borrowed from Proto-Saka, possibly from *Yehāñä, perhaps from *yehāñä (“cleaned, healed”), compare Khotanese gyehāña, jehuña (“cleaned, healed”). Parallel borrowing with Ancient Greek Ζειονίσης (Zeionísēs).

Borrowed from Proto-Saka, possibly from *Yehāñakä, perhaps from *yehāñä (“cleaned, healed”) + *-ki (hypocoristic suffix), compare Khotanese gyehāña, jehuña (“cleaned, healed”). Parallel borrowing with Ancient Greek Ζειονίσης (Zeionísēs).
From Proto-Saka *Diyāka (“supervisor”). Compare with Khotanese dai, di (“to see”).
Borrowed from Ancient Greek Δημήτριος (Dēmḗtrios).

column5: protector of the religion; religion; to protect
column6: From Proto-Saka *Dainapavā (“protector of the religion”), composed of a cognate of Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬉𐬥𐬁 (daēnā, “religion”) + a cognate of Khotanese pā (“to protect”).

column5: given by deva􂀿s􂁀; given by deva[s]
column6: Inherited from Sanskrit देवदत्त (devadatta, “given by deva[s]”).

column5: begotten by the creator; creator; born
column6: From Proto-Saka *Dāmizāta (literally “begotten by the creator”), composed of a cognate of Avestan 𐬛𐬁𐬨𐬀𐬫 (dāmay, “creator”) + a cognate of Khotanese ysāta (“born”). Compare with Avestan 𐬛𐬁𐬨𐬌𐬛𐬁𐬙𐬀 (dāmi.dāta), Old Persian *Dāmidātaʰ, and Parthian 𐭃…
From Proto-Saka *Namarauda (“worship-heightening”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese nauda (“obeisance, worship”) + Proto-Saka *raud (“to grow”) (compare with Khotanese rruv (“to grow”)).
From Proto-Saka *nada (“leader”). Compare with Khotanese nada (“leader”).
From Middle Persian 𐭭𐭥𐭮𐭧𐭩 (nrshw /⁠Narisah, Narseh⁠/) + -𐨐 (-ka).

column5: protector of the clan; navel; keeper; to protect
column6: From Proto-Saka *Nahapāna (“protector of the clan”), composed of a term cognate with Khotanese nāha (“navel”) + a term cognate with Khotanese pānä (“keeper”), pā (“to protect”). Cognate with Prakrit 𑀦𑀳𑀧𑀸𑀦 (nahapāna).

column5: servant-girl of God/the Lord; lord; to look; observer
column6: From Proto-Saka *Bagaspasi (literally “servant-girl of God/the Lord”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese vvūv (“lord”), from Iranian *Baga (compare with Old Persian 𐏎 (Baga)) + a cognate of Khotanese spaśś (“to look”), spaśa (“observer”). Compare with the ot…
From Proto-Saka *padika (“leader”). Compare with Khotanese patä, patäna (“before, in front of”).
From Proto-Saka *mayaka (“prosperous”) (compare with Khotanese ggumai (“at will”)). Compare with 𐨨𐨆𐨀 (moa) and 𐨨𐨆𐨒 (moga).
Borrowed from Ancient Greek Μένανδρος (Ménandros).
From Proto-Saka *Mavyaka, from *mavya (“tiger, hero”) (compare with Khotanese mauya, muyi (“tiger”); Sogdian 𐼺𐼷𐼴 (myw), 𐫖𐫏𐫇 (myw, “tiger”)). Compare with 𐨨𐨆𐨀 (moa) and 𐨨𐨆𐨒 (moga).
From Proto-Saka *mava (“hero, tiger”) (cf. Khotanese mauya, muyi (“tiger”); Sogdian 𐼺𐼷𐼴 (myu), 𐫖𐫏𐫇 (myu, “tiger”)).
From Proto-Saka *mauka (“hero, tiger”) (compare with Khotanese mauya, muyi (“tiger”); Sogdian 𐼺𐼷𐼴 (myu), 𐫖𐫏𐫇 (myu, “tiger”)). Cognate with Ancient Greek Μαύης (Maúēs); compare with 𐨨𐨅𐨬𐨐𐨁 (mevaki).
From Proto-Saka *maja (“delightful”), cognate with Khotanese māja (“delightful”).
From Proto-Saka *Mānyakula (“delightful progeny”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese mānya (“delighted”) + a cognate of Khotanese kula (“progeny”).
Inherited from Sanskrit मदन (madana, “sexual love, passion; delighting; Kāma”). Cognate with Pali madana, Prakrit 𑀫𑀬𑀡 (mayaṇa)

column5: ruling king; directing, ruling, ruler; to direct, rule; ruling, ruler; excellent, strong; ruler
column6: From Proto-Saka *Rāzavara (“ruling king”), composed of *rāza (“directing, ruling, ruler”) (cf. Khotanese rrays (“to direct, rule”), rraysa (official title), *razaka (“ruling, ruler”) + *vara (“excellent, strong”) (cf. Khotanese vara (“excellent, strong”), Toch…
From Proto-Saka *ryaka (“youth”) (compare with Khotanese rya (“youth”)). Cognate with Ancient Greek Λιακο (Liako).

column6: From an earlier form *Vayaspasi, ultimately from Proto-Saka *Bagaspasa (literally “servant of God/the Lord”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese vvūv (“lord”), from Iranian *Baga (cf. Old Persian 𐏎 (Baga)) + a cognate of Khotanese spaśś (“to look”), spaśa (“o…

column5: servant of God/the Lord; lord; to look; observer
column6: From an earlier form *Vayaspasika, ultimately from Proto-Saka *Bagaspasika (literally “servant of God/the Lord”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese vvūv (“lord”), from Iranian *Baga (cf. Old Persian 𐏎 (Baga)) + a cognate of Khotanese spaśś (“to look”), spaśa…
Borrowed from Proto-Saka. See cognate Prakrit 𑀰𑁄𑀤𑀸𑀲 (śodāsa) for etymology.

column5: commander of army; army; desiring, commanding; to desire
column6: From Proto-Saka *Spalarīźa (“commander of army”), composed of *spala (“army”), itself from Parthian 𐭏𐭎𐭐𐭀𐭃 (ispāδ, “army”) (cf. Old Persian 𐎿𐎱𐎠𐎭 (spāda, “army”))) + *rīźa (“desiring, commanding”) (cf. Khotanese rriś (“to desire”), Sogdian 𐽀𐼷𐼵𐼸𐽀𐼰…

column5: most desired; desired; to desire, wish
column6: Borrowed from Proto-Saka, possibly from *Spalakātamä, perhaps from *Spalä (tribe name) + *kātamä (“most desired”), from Proto-Iranian *kaHtamah, superlative *kaHtáh (“desired”) (whence Younger Avestan 𐬐𐬁𐬙𐬀 (kāta)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kaHtás, from Pro…

column5: commander of army; army; leader, commander
column6: From Proto-Saka *Spalahaura (“commander of army”), composed of *spala (“army”), itself from Parthian 𐭏𐭎𐭐𐭀𐭃 (ispāδ, “army”) (cf. Old Persian 𐎿𐎱𐎠𐎭 (spāda, “army”))) + *haura (“leader, commander”) (cf. Khotanese haura (“leader, commander”)).
Borrowed from Ancient Greek Στράτων (Strátōn).
Borrowed from Ancient Greek Ζωΐλος (Zōḯlos).

column5: famous by birth; birth, origin; name
column6: From Proto-Saka *Zātanāman (literally “famous by birth”), composed of a cognate of Khotanese ysā and Sanskrit जातम् (jātam, “birth, origin”) + a cognate of Khotanese nāma (“name”).
From a Proto-Saka [Term?] name meaning "rich in gifts", composed of a cognate of Khotanese hora, haura (“gift”) + a cognate of Khotanese tsāta (“rich”) or a borrowing from Parthian or Bactrian sād.

column5: helper, companion; riding together; to ride
column6: From Proto-Saka *hadabāra (“helper, companion”, literally “riding together”) (cf. Khotanese bār (“to ride”)).
From Proto-Iranian *HáHtr̥daHtah. Equivalent to 𐬁𐬙𐬆𐬭𐬆 (ātər^ə, “fire”) + 𐬛𐬁𐬙𐬀 (dāta, “given, created”). Cognate with Old Persian *Ātr̥dātah and *Āçidātah.

column5: Fire; fire; protected; to protect; fire
column6: From Proto-Iranian *HaHtr̥paHtah, from *HáHtr̥š (“Fire; fire”) + *paHtáh (“protected”), from Proto-Iranian *paHtáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *paHtás, from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂-tó-s, from *peh₂- (“to protect”) + *-tós.
From 𐬐𐬀𐬎𐬎𐬌 (kauui, “poet, bard”) + -𐬁𐬙𐬀 (-āta, hypocoristic suffix).
From 𐬬𐬌𐬱𐬙𐬀 (višta, “free, unbridled”) + 𐬀𐬯𐬞𐬀 (aspa, “horse”). Cognate with Sanskrit विषित अश्व (víṣita-áśva).
From 𐬵𐬎- (hu-, “good”) + 𐬀𐬯𐬞𐬀 (aspa, “horse”). Cognate of Old Persian *Huvaspah, Sanskrit स्वश्व॑ (sváśva), and Ancient Greek Εὔϊππος (Eúïppos).
From earlier *Aryabr̥zāh. Cognate with Old Persian *Aryabr̥zāh.
From Proto-Iranian *(W)ŕ̥šakah, from *(w)ŕ̥šā (“man, hero”) + *-kah (hypocoristic suffix). Cognate with Old Persian 𐎠𐎼𐏁𐎣 (R̥šakaʰ).
From earlier *R̥tabānuš, cognate with Old Persian *R̥tabānuš and Sanskrit अतपान (atapāna).
From earlier *R̥tapānah, cognate with Old Persian *R̥tapānah and Sanskrit अतपान (atapāna).
From earlier *Gautarzah, from Proto-Iranian *gā́wš (“ox”) + *tárjayati (“to crush”).
From earlier *Valagašah, with the approximate meaning "having joy as desired".

column5: beautiful growth; growth; appearance; face; good; growth
column6: The origin is uncertain. Likely from a compound whose second part is cognate with Avestan 𐬭𐬀𐬊𐬜𐬀 (raoδa, “growth; appearance”), Persian روی (roy, “face”), with one proposed but uncertain etymology being Old Persian *hurauda- (“beautiful growth”), from *hu-…
From Avestan 𐬬𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬚𐬭𐬀𐬖𐬥𐬀 (vər^əθraγna, “Verethragna”), from Proto-Iranian *Wr̥tragnáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Wr̥tragʰnás. Compare Middle Persian 𐭥𐭫𐭧𐭫𐭠𐭭 (ʿlḥlʾn /⁠Warahrām, Warahrān, Wahrām⁠/).
From earlier *Manaicah, cognate with Old Persian *Manaicah, and composed of *manah (“mind”) + *-icah (hypocoristic suffix).
From earlier *Miθradātah. Compare with Old Persian *Miθradātah.
From earlier *Naryasanhah, cognate with Avestan *𐬥𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬋⸱𐬯𐬀𐬓𐬀 (*naⁱriiō.saxᵛa), variant of 𐬥𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬋⸱𐬯𐬀𐬢𐬵𐬀 (naⁱriiō.saŋha, “Nairyosangha”, literally “potent utterance”), name of a yazata.
From Proto-Iranian [Term?]. Compare Avestan 𐬯𐬞𐬆𐬧𐬙𐬋𐬜𐬁𐬙𐬀 (spəṇtōδāta), Old Persian *Spantadātah, Old Armenian Սպանդարատ (Spandarat), Modern Persian اسپنداد (espandâd), سپنداد (sepandâd).

Cognate with Middle Persian 𐭯𐭪𐭥𐭥𐭩 (pkwry /⁠Pakur⁠/). Of uncertain origin. According to Schmitt, perhaps a hypocoristic from Old Iranian *Pak-ura- formed from the root *pak- (“to cook”), whence Persian پختن (poxtan).
From earlier *Frahātah, from Proto-Iranian *fra- (“toward, forward”) + *haHtah (“earned, acquired”).

From earlier *Fryapatiš, from Proto-Iranian *FriHyápatiš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *PriHyápatiš, from *priHyás (“beloved”) + *pátiš (“master”). Cognate with Old Persian *Fryapatiš, and Sanskrit प्रियपति (priyápati).
Akin to Old Armenian Երաստ (Erast), Արաստ (Arast), Iranian borrowings.
Borrowed from Middle Persian 𐭱𐭧𐭯𐭥𐭧𐭥𐭩 (šḥpwḥry /⁠Šābuhr⁠/).
From earlier *Tīradātah. Compare Persian تیرداد (tirdâd).
From earlier *Tīrīdātah. Compare Ancient Greek Τιριδάτης (Tiridátēs).

Inherited from Old Persian *R̥taxšaθrah. The genuine Middle Persian development of Old Persian 𐎠𐎼𐎫𐎧𐏁𐏂𐎠 (Artaxšaçā) would be *Ardašas. Compare Sanskrit ऋतक्षयर्ष (ṛtakṣayarṣa), अर्तक्षयर्ष (artakṣayarṣa).

column5: man; He who has men and horses; Orodes
column6: Uncertain. Usually treated as a hypocoristic formation with the suffix + *-ōē from a name with *wiHrás (“man”), such as Avestan 𐬬𐬍𐬭𐬁𐬯𐬞𐬀 (vīrāspa, “He who has men and horses”). In the ŠKZ inscription corresponds to Parthian 𐭅𐭓𐭅𐭃 (wrwd, “Orodes”), so…
Ultimately from Avestan 𐬬𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬚𐬭𐬀𐬖𐬥𐬀 (vər^əθraγna), from Proto-Iranian *Wr̥tragnáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Wr̥tragʰnás. Compare Parthian 𐭅𐭓𐭉𐭇𐭓𐭌 (wryḥrm /⁠Wahrām⁠/, “war god, god of victory”).
Akin to Old Armenian Երաստ (Erast), Արաստ (Arast), Iranian borrowings.
From Old Persian *Naryasanhah itself inherited from Proto-Iranian *Hnárācánhah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hnárāćánsas.

From Avestan 𐬥𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬋⸱𐬯𐬀𐬢𐬵𐬀 (naⁱriiō.saŋha), itself inherited from Proto-Iranian *Hnárācánhah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hnárāćánsas. Doublet of 𐭭𐭥𐭮𐭧𐭩 (nrsḥy /⁠Narseh⁠⁠/), compare with Old Persian *Naryasanhah.
From Old Persian *Pāpakah. Equivalent to 𐭯𐭠𐭯𐭩 (pʾpy /⁠Pāb⁠/) + -𐭪𐭩 (-ky, hypocoristic suffix). Cognate with Old Armenian Պապ (Pap), պապ (pap), which are Iranian borrowings.

From Parthian 𐭐𐭓𐭂𐭅𐭆 (prgwz /⁠Paryōž⁠/), itself from Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌⸱𐬀𐬊𐬘𐬀𐬵 (paⁱri.aojah), composed of 𐬞𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌 (paⁱri, “around”) + 𐬀𐬊𐬘𐬀𐬵 (aojah, “strength, power”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pari, from Proto-Indo-European *péri + Proto-Indo-I…

From earlier *Šāhpuhr, from Old Persian *xšāyaθiyahyāpuθrah (literally “king's son”), from 𐏋 (XŠ /⁠xšāyaθiyaʰ⁠/, “king”) + *puθrah (“son”).
From 𐰋𐰃𐰠 (b²il² /⁠bil-⁠/, “to know”) + 𐰏𐰀- (g²a- /⁠-ge⁠/).
From Classical Persian رمضان (ramazān), from Arabic رَمَضَان (ramaḍān)
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *āk (“white; bright”). Perhaps related to Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐾁 (ʾʾl /⁠al⁠/, “red”).

column5: heavy; to rise, to elevate; pain, ache; illness; load, difficulty
column6: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *agïr (“heavy”), possibly an old derivation from (Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽲𐽹𐽰𐽲 (ʾʾqmʾq /⁠aġ-⁠/, “to rise, to elevate”)) or alternatively related to Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽲𐽾𐽶𐽲 (ʾʾqryq /⁠aġrïġ⁠/, “pain, ache; illness”) and Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽲𐽾…
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *āy (“the Moon, month”).

column6: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *adā (“danger; hindrance”), though not attested elsewhere on its own.
Borrowed from Classical Syriac ܐܕܡ (ʾdm, “Adam”), via Parthian 𐭀𐭃𐭀𐭌 (ʾdʾm /⁠ādām⁠/) and Sogdian 𐫀𐫔𐫀𐫖 (ʾδʾm, “idem”).

Inherited from Proto-Turkic *adut (“palm of the hand; handful”). Cognate with Karakhanid اَذُتْ (ʾaḏut).
Inherited from Proto-Common Turkic *adïg (“bear”).

column5: quiet, peaceful; to be quiet, mild, calm; to be amicable
column6: By surface analysis, *𐽰𐽰𐽹𐽹𐽰𐽲 (*ʾʾmmʾq /⁠*am-⁠/) + -𐽶𐾁 (-yl /⁠-ïl⁠/), inherited from Proto-Turkic *amïl (“quiet, peaceful”) (from Proto-Turkic *am- (“to be quiet, mild, calm; to be amicable”)). Also found in Karakhanid اَمُلْ (ʾamul· /⁠amul⁠/).
A rendering of Middle Chinese 安 ('an).
Borrowed from Sogdian 𐼰𐼰𐼿𐼰𐽀𐼷 (ʾʾcʾry), from Sanskrit आ॒चा॒र्य॑ (ācāryà, “spiritual guide or teacher”).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *(h)āl (“red, crimson”).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *(h)āla (“dapple, freckle; variegated”). Relation to 𐽰𐽰𐾁 (al, “red, vermilion”), if any, is unclear and morphologically obscure.

column5: large tent; nomadic tent; tent; nomad's hut
column6: Unknown. Also found in Karakhanid اَلَجُو (ʾalajuw /⁠alaçu⁠/, “large tent”), Chagatai الاچوق (ʾlʾcwq /⁠alaçuḳ⁠/, “nomadic tent”), Kipchak alatſuc (alaçuḳ, “tent”) and Ottoman Turkish آلاچق (ʾlʾjq /⁠alacuḳ⁠/, “nomad's hut”).
By surface analysis, 𐽰𐽰𐾁𐽲𐽰𐽹𐽰𐽲 (ʾʾlqʾmʾq /⁠alḳa-⁠/) + -𐾀 (-t /⁠-t⁠/) + -𐽹𐽶𐽿 (-myš /⁠-mïş⁠/), derived from Proto-Turkic *alka- (“to praise, to exalt”).

column5: gold; bronze; crimson, vermilion; red, vermilion
column6: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *altūn (“gold”); possibly derived from Middle Chinese 銅 (duwng, “bronze”) with an unknown first component, perhaps 𐽰𐽰𐾁 (ʾʾl /⁠al⁠/, “crimson, vermilion”). A similar semantic relation exists in the Chinese term as well, related to…

column5: child 􂀿of any gender􂁀; son; child [of any gender]; son
column6: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *ogul (“child [of any gender]; son”). Cognate with Orkhon Turkic 𐰆𐰍𐰞 (wg¹l¹ /⁠oġul⁠/) and Karakhanid اُغُل (oğul).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *ȫŕ (“self”). Cognate with Orkhon Turkic 𐰇𐰔 (ẅz /⁠öz⁠/), Karakhanid اُوزْ (ȫz).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *ōn (“ten”). Cognate with Orkhon Turkic 𐰆𐰣 (wn¹ /⁠on⁠/) and Karakhanid اُونْ (on).
Borrowed from Middle Chinese 貽 (yi).

column5: man; to be, copular verb; virtue; Christian
column6: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *ēr (“man”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰼 (r² /⁠er⁠/) and Karakhanid اَرْ (er).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *alp (“difficult; brazen, brave; heroic warrior”).
From Proto-Common Turkic *kaya (“rock, boulder”). Cognate with Yakut хайа (xaya) and Ottoman Turkish قیا (kaya).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *kara (“black”). Cognate with Orkhon Turkic 𐰴𐰺𐰀 (k¹r¹a /⁠qara⁠/) and Karakhanid قَرا (qara).
Borrowed from Middle Chinese 公主 (kuwng tsyu^X, “daughter of a monarch, princess”). Not attested after 11ᵗʰ century.
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *kï̄ŕ (“girl”). Cognate with Orkhon Turkic 𐰶𐰃𐰕 (ik¹iz /⁠qïz⁠/) and Karakhanid قٖيزْ (qï̄z).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *yürek (“heart”). Cognate with Karakhanid يُرَكْ (yüräk).

column5: to shine; to shine, to illuminate
column6: By surface analysis, 𐽶𐽰𐽾𐽳𐽹𐽰𐽲 (yʾrwmʾq /⁠yaru-⁠/, “to shine, to illuminate”) + -𐽷 (-k /⁠-ḳ⁠/, deverbal suffix), from Proto-Turkic *yaru- (“to shine”).
By surface analysis, 𐽼𐽰𐽽𐽰𐽹𐽰𐽲 (pʾcʾmʾq /⁠bača-⁠/, “to fast”) + -𐽷 (-k /⁠-ḳ⁠/, deverbal suffix), further derived from Proto-Turkic *bača- (“to fast”). Cognate with Karakhanid بَجاقْ (“Christian fast”).

column5: protector of the clan; navel; keeper; to protect
column6: Borrowed from Proto-Saka *Nahapāna (“protector of the clan”), composed of a term cognate with Khotanese nāha (“navel”) + a term cognate with Khotanese pānä (“keeper”), pā (“to protect”). Cognate with Gandhari 𐨣𐨱𐨤𐨣 (nahapana).
